lede:
Round 3 tested additional GSLC dates, a gradient loss and longer training. Settings were selected on round 2’s validation frames before evaluation on the test regions. Training used batches of 16; scoring ran on CPU.

Listing GSLC files directly fixed the round 2 download failures and raised the median number of extra dates from 5 to 8. Gradient loss gave a small accuracy gain without sharper output. Extending training to 8,000 steps also helped slightly.
gslc:
Step 1: more GSLC dates per tile

Round 2 guessed each GSLC file name from its GCOV twin and stopped at 5 extra dates. Round 3 lists every 40 MHz GSLC granule per track and frame from NASA CMR (full and partial frames) and reads up to 10 extra dates per tile, retrying transient errors. File lookup corrected (0 of 4,044 reads failed); they came from the guessed names, not from missing data. The median tile now averages 8 extra dates (7 looks per pixel, up from 5). Tiles with at least 3 dates over 90% of their area rose from 292 to 351 of 468. Coverage is still uneven. Melbourne (1 GSLC in the archive) and Shandong (2) get no extra dates, and on Johannesburg, north Taiwan and São Paulo many repeats are partial frames that miss the tile ("outside window" below).

The expanded reference changed the results little. Retraining on it left far-region MAE at 2.065 dB and slightly improved near-region and validation errors. Fine-detail energy fell from 0.30 to 0.28 in the far group: additional reference dates did not make the L1-trained output sharper.
loss:
Step 2: gradient-L1 for the multi-date target

We added an L1 term on Sobel x and y gradients (prediction against target, valid pixels only) to the multi-date model's loss, at weights 0.5 and 1.0. The rule, fixed in advance: on validation against the multi-date target, count wins over plain L1 on MAE, SSIM, detail correlation and both chamfers, and break ties with the higher fine-detail energy (sharper). Both weights won 3 of 5 (MAE, detail correlation, invented edges); weight 0.5 was selected on sharpness. The winner and plain L1 then got a second seed each.

Across two seeds the effect is consistent but small, with a tradeoff in sharpness. Against the multi-date target, gradient-L1 lowers MAE (far 1.373 to 1.374 vs 1.397 to 1.398 dB; near 0.95 vs 0.98) and invents fewer edges (12.6 vs 13.3 m far). It also lowers the grid imprint (2.10 vs 2.22) and nudges detail correlation up (0.343 to 0.344 vs 0.339 to 0.340). But it is not sharper: fine-detail energy falls slightly (0.39 vs 0.40), SSIM drops (0.493 vs 0.499 to 0.500) and missed edges rise (14.5 to 14.6 vs 13.8 to 13.9 m). The seed spread is at most 0.004 on the scores and 0.6 m on chamfer, so these differences are real but small. Matching target gradients in L1 still rewards the conditional median: gradients that L1 cannot place are averaged away. Round 4 below tests an adversarial term.
long:
Step 3: round 1 length (8,000 steps)

We reran the round 2 winner (consistency 0.5 at 40 m) and the multi-date model at 8,000 steps, against 3,000 in round 2. Both improve a little. Against the single-date target on far tiles, the winner's MAE goes from 1.719 to 1.707 dB, detail correlation from 0.327 to 0.332 and grid imprint from 2.41 to 2.22. It still beats bicubic on all five far metrics. On near tiles its grid imprint also falls (4.36 to 3.76), while missed edges rise slightly. The multi-date model's grid imprint drops from 2.08 to 1.91 and its detail correlation rises from 0.322 to 0.326. The rankings between models do not change, so round 2's shorter runs did not distort its conclusions.
caveats:
• Round 3 shared the GPU with Experiment 5 under a memory gate. One run (r3_g1_s0) was killed during a memory spill and rerun from scratch; no reported number comes from an interrupted run.
  • Two seeds is the minimum for a seed check. The step 2 differences exceed the seed spread, but only by a few hundredths of a dB.
  • The deeper GSLC target is still uneven across frames. Holdout 5 m scores cover 29 far and 29 near tiles, from Buenos Aires, Johannesburg, Abu Dhabi and north Taiwan; Melbourne has no GSLC repeats.
  • The plain-L1 seed 0 run is round 2's m_multi (same settings, unseeded), reused to save GPU time.
